title.de: Mehr Relativsätze: who mit Komma, whose, whom

title.it: Altre relative: who con la virgola, whose, whom

goal.sl: Dodaš podatek o komer koli z vejicama (Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, …), rabiš whose, whom in in which ter which za cel stavek.
goal.de: Du fügst mit Kommas etwas über jemanden hinzu (Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, …), nimmst whose, whom und in which und which für einen ganzen Satz.
goal.it: Aggiungi qualcosa su qualcuno con le virgole (Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, …), usi whose, whom e in which, e which per una frase intera.
goal.en: You can add something about someone with commas (Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, …), and use whose, whom, in which, and which for a whole sentence.

say.sl: Z vejicama stavek doda nekaj o osebi, ki jo že poznaš: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, is our blacksmith.** (Gospod Dixon, ki živi ob potoku, je naš kovač.) Če ga izpustiš, še vedno veš, kdo je. Brez vejic pove, katera oseba: **The man who lives by the beck is our blacksmith.** Slovenščina piše vejico v obeh, angleščina samo v prvem.
say.de: Mit Kommas fügt der Satz etwas über jemanden hinzu, den du schon kennst: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, is our blacksmith.** (Mr Dixon, der am Bach wohnt, ist unser Schmied.) Lässt du ihn weg, weißt du noch, wer es ist. Ohne Kommas sagt er, welche Person: **The man who lives by the beck is our blacksmith.** Deutsch hat in beiden ein Komma, Englisch nur im ersten.
say.it: Con le virgole la frase aggiunge qualcosa su una persona che conosci già: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, is our blacksmith.** (Mr Dixon, che abita vicino al torrente, è il nostro fabbro.) Se la togli, sai ancora chi è. Senza virgole dice quale persona: **The man who lives by the beck is our blacksmith.**
say.en: With commas the clause adds something about someone you already know: **Mr Dixon, who lives by the beck, is our blacksmith.** Take it out and you still know who he is. With no commas it says which person: **The man who lives by the beck is our blacksmith.**

say.sl: Vejici spremenita pomen: **Edna's son, who lives in Keswick, is a baker.** (En sin.) **Edna's son who lives in Keswick is a baker.** (Več sinov.) Z vejicama sina samo opišeš, brez njih ga izbereš med drugimi. V govoru se to sliši kot kratek premor.
say.de: Die Kommas ändern den Sinn: **Edna's son, who lives in Keswick, is a baker.** (Ein Sohn.) **Edna's son who lives in Keswick is a baker.** (Mehrere Söhne.) Mit Kommas beschreibst du den Sohn, ohne sie wählst du ihn aus. Gesprochen hört man eine kurze Pause.
say.it: Le virgole cambiano il senso: **Edna's son, who lives in Keswick, is a baker.** (Un figlio.) **Edna's son who lives in Keswick is a baker.** (Più figli.) Con le virgole descrivi il figlio, senza lo scegli tra gli altri. A voce si sente una breve pausa.
say.en: The commas change the meaning: **Edna's son, who lives in Keswick, is a baker.** (One son.) **Edna's son who lives in Keswick is a baker.** (More than one.) With commas you describe him; with none you pick him out from the others. In talk you hear a short pause.

say.sl: Za stvari in kraje rabiš **which**: **The mill, which was built in 1800, is closed now.** (Mlin, ki je bil zgrajen leta 1800, je zdaj zaprt.) Za vejico pisava hoče **who** ali **which**; **that** ostane za stavke brez vejic. Tudi kot predmet beseda ostane: **Hill Top, which we visited last year, is near Sawrey.** (Hill Top, ki smo ga obiskali lani, je blizu Sawreyja.)
say.de: Für Dinge und Orte nimmst du **which**: **The mill, which was built in 1800, is closed now.** (Die Mühle, die 1800 gebaut wurde, ist jetzt geschlossen.) Nach dem Komma steht geschrieben **who** oder **which**; **that** bleibt für Sätze ohne Kommas. Auch als Objekt bleibt das Wort: **Hill Top, which we visited last year, is near Sawrey.** (Hill Top, das wir letztes Jahr besucht haben, liegt bei Sawrey.)
say.it: Per cose e luoghi usi **which**: **The mill, which was built in 1800, is closed now.** (Il mulino, che fu costruito nel 1800, ora è chiuso.) Dopo la virgola, per iscritto, si usa **who** o **which**; **that** resta per le frasi senza virgole. Anche come oggetto la parola resta: **Hill Top, which we visited last year, is near Sawrey.** (Hill Top, che abbiamo visitato l'anno scorso, è vicino a Sawrey.)
say.en: For things and places use **which**: **The mill, which was built in 1800, is closed now.** After a comma writing wants **who** or **which**; **that** stays for clauses with no commas. Even as the object the word stays: **Hill Top, which we visited last year, is near Sawrey.**

examples.de: Die Mühle, die 1800 gebaut wurde, ist jetzt geschlossen.
examples.it: Il mulino, che fu costruito nel 1800, ora è chiuso.

say.sl: **whose** stoji za his, her, its, their, tudi z vejicama: **Old Wilf, whose dog died last year, lives alone.** (Stari Wilf, ki mu je lani poginil pes, živi sam.) **Mrs Birkett, whose son plays football, runs the inn.** Rabiš ga tudi za stvari: **The mill, whose wheel is broken, is for sale.** Sliši se kot *who's* (who is), a piše se drugače.
say.de: **whose** steht für his, her, its, their, auch mit Kommas: **Old Wilf, whose dog died last year, lives alone.** (Der alte Wilf, dessen Hund letztes Jahr gestorben ist, lebt allein.) **Mrs Birkett, whose son plays football, runs the inn.** Es geht auch für Dinge: **The mill, whose wheel is broken, is for sale.** Es klingt wie *who's* (who is), wird aber anders geschrieben.
say.it: **whose** sta per his, her, its, their, anche con le virgole: **Old Wilf, whose dog died last year, lives alone.** (Il vecchio Wilf, il cui cane è morto l'anno scorso, vive da solo.) **Mrs Birkett, whose son plays football, runs the inn.** Va bene anche per le cose: **The mill, whose wheel is broken, is for sale.** Suona come *who's* (who is), ma si scrive diverso.
say.en: **whose** stands for his, her, its, their, with commas too: **Old Wilf, whose dog died last year, lives alone.** **Mrs Birkett, whose son plays football, runs the inn.** It works for things as well: **The mill, whose wheel is broken, is for sale.** It sounds like *who's* (who is), but it's spelt differently.

say.sl: V govoru predlog ostane na koncu: **Mr Tyson, who I spoke to yesterday, was very kind.** V uradni pisavi gre naprej, za njim **whom** ali **which**: **Mr Tyson, to whom I spoke yesterday, was very kind.** (Gospod Tyson, s katerim sem včeraj {m:govoril|f:govorila}, je bil zelo prijazen.) **the house in which she was born**. Ljudje rečejo tudi *to who*; pisava hoče **whom**.
say.de: Gesprochen bleibt die Präposition am Ende: **Mr Tyson, who I spoke to yesterday, was very kind.** Förmlich steht sie vorn, danach **whom** oder **which**: **Mr Tyson, to whom I spoke yesterday, was very kind.** (Mr Tyson, mit dem ich gestern gesprochen habe, war sehr freundlich.) **the house in which she was born**. Man sagt auch *to who*; geschrieben steht **whom**.
say.it: A voce la preposizione resta in fondo: **Mr Tyson, who I spoke to yesterday, was very kind.** Nello scritto formale va davanti, poi **whom** o **which**: **Mr Tyson, to whom I spoke yesterday, was very kind.** (Mr Tyson, con cui ho parlato ieri, è stato molto gentile.) **the house in which she was born**. Si dice anche *to who*; per iscritto si usa **whom**.
say.en: In talk the small word stays at the end: **Mr Tyson, who I spoke to yesterday, was very kind.** Formal writing puts it first, then **whom** or **which**: **Mr Tyson, to whom I spoke yesterday, was very kind.** **the house in which she was born**. People also say *to who*; writing wants **whom**.

say.sl: **which** lahko stoji za cel stavek, kot slovenski *kar*: **The van broke down, which was a pity.** **Jack came late, which isn't like him.** (Jack je prišel pozno, kar mu ni podobno.) Ljudje rečejo tudi *what was a pity*; pisava hoče **which**. Za številom: **forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks**, **two sons, both of whom live here**.
say.de: **which** kann für einen ganzen Satz stehen, wie das deutsche was: **The van broke down, which was a pity.** **Jack came late, which isn't like him.** (Jack kam spät, was gar nicht zu ihm passt.) Man sagt auch *what was a pity*; geschrieben steht **which**. Nach einer Zahl: **forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks**, **two sons, both of whom live here**.
say.it: **which** può stare per una frase intera, come *il che*: **The van broke down, which was a pity.** **Jack came late, which isn't like him.** (Jack è arrivato tardi, il che non è da lui.) Si dice anche *what was a pity*; per iscritto si usa **which**. Dopo un numero: **forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks**, **two sons, both of whom live here**.
say.en: **which** can stand for a whole sentence: **The van broke down, which was a pity.** **Jack came late, which isn't like him.** People also say *what was a pity*; writing wants **which**. After a number: **forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks**, **two sons, both of whom live here**.

translation.sl: Keswick, ki je osem milj stran, ima ob sobotah tržnico. Gospa Birkett, ki ima gostilno na trati, gre tja vsak teden. Njena sestra, ki živi v Keswicku, se dobi z njo na čaju. Samov kombi, ki je zelo star, ju pelje domov. Arthur, čigar čebele delajo med, ga tam prodaja. Gospod Tyson, čigar mlin je zdaj zaprt, kupuje oves. Stari Wilf, ki ga vsi imamo radi, pripoveduje zgodbe pod hrastom. Pogosto dežuje, kar nikogar ne moti.
translation.de: Keswick, das acht Meilen entfernt ist, hat samstags Markt. Mrs Birkett, deren Gasthaus am Dorfplatz liegt, fährt jede Woche hin. Ihre Schwester, die in Keswick wohnt, trifft sie zum Tee. Sams Lieferwagen, der sehr alt ist, bringt sie heim. Arthur, dessen Bienen den Honig machen, verkauft ihn dort. Mr Tyson, dessen Mühle jetzt geschlossen ist, kauft Hafer. Der alte Wilf, den wir alle gernhaben, erzählt unter der Eiche Geschichten. Es regnet oft, was niemanden stört.
translation.it: Keswick, che è a otto miglia, ha il mercato al sabato. Mrs Birkett, la cui locanda è sul prato, ci va ogni settimana. Sua sorella, che abita a Keswick, la incontra per il tè. Il furgone di Sam, che è molto vecchio, le riporta a casa. Arthur, le cui api fanno il miele, lo vende lì. Mr Tyson, il cui mulino ora è chiuso, compra l'avena. Il vecchio Wilf, a cui vogliamo tutti bene, racconta storie sotto la quercia. Piove spesso, il che non dà fastidio a nessuno.
translation.en: Keswick, which is eight miles away, has a market on Saturdays. Mrs Birkett, whose inn is on the green, goes there every week. Her sister, who lives in Keswick, meets her for tea. Sam's van, which is very old, takes them home. Arthur, whose bees make the honey, sells it there. Mr Tyson, whose mill is closed now, buys oats. Old Wilf, who we all love, tells stories under the oak. It often rains, which nobody minds.

exercises.text: We've got forty sheep, most of ___ are Herdwicks. Mr Tyson has two sons, both of ___ live in Kendal. Jack left the gate open, ___ made Mr Tyson very cross. Harry, ___ mum runs the inn, loves football. Arthur, to ___ we sold the hives, was very pleased. Windermere, ___ is the largest lake in England, is full of boats.

accept: which
whom
which
whose
whom
which

translation.sl: Imamo štirideset ovc, večinoma pasme herdwick. Gospod Tyson ima dva sinova, oba živita v Kendalu. Jack je pustil vrata odprta, kar je gospoda Tysona zelo razjezilo. Harry, čigar mama vodi gostilno, ima rad nogomet. Arthur, ki smo mu prodali panje, je bil zelo vesel. Windermere, ki je največje jezero v Angliji, je polno čolnov.
translation.de: Wir haben vierzig Schafe, die meisten davon Herdwicks. Mr Tyson hat zwei Söhne, die beide in Kendal wohnen. Jack hat das Tor offen gelassen, was Mr Tyson sehr geärgert hat. Harry, dessen Mutter das Gasthaus führt, liebt Fußball. Arthur, dem wir die Bienenstöcke verkauft haben, hat sich sehr gefreut. Windermere, der größte See Englands, ist voller Boote.
translation.it: Abbiamo quaranta pecore, la maggior parte delle quali Herdwick. Mr Tyson ha due figli, che abitano entrambi a Kendal. Jack ha lasciato il cancello aperto, il che ha fatto molto arrabbiare Mr Tyson. Harry, la cui mamma gestisce la locanda, ama il calcio. Arthur, a cui abbiamo venduto le arnie, è stato molto contento. Il Windermere, che è il lago più grande d'Inghilterra, è pieno di barche.
translation.en: We've got forty sheep, most of which are Herdwicks. Mr Tyson has two sons, both of whom live in Kendal. Jack left the gate open, which made Mr Tyson very cross. Harry, whose mum runs the inn, loves football. Arthur, to whom we sold the hives, was very pleased. Windermere, which is the largest lake in England, is full of boats.

exercises.text: Keswick, ___ is eight miles from here, has a pencil museum. Mr Dixon, ___ smithy is by the beck, made our gate. Edna, ___ everybody knows, talks all day. The bus was late, ___ made us cross. Mrs Birkett, to ___ I gave the letter, says thank you.

accept: which
whose
who
whom
which
whom

translation.sl: Keswick, ki je osem milj od tukaj, ima muzej svinčnikov. Gospod Dixon, ki ima kovačnico ob potoku, je naredil naša vrata. Edna, ki jo vsi poznajo, govori ves dan. Avtobus je zamujal, kar nas je razjezilo. Gospa Birkett, ki sem ji {m:dal|f:dala} pismo, se zahvaljuje.
translation.de: Keswick, das acht Meilen von hier entfernt ist, hat ein Bleistiftmuseum. Mr Dixon, dessen Schmiede am Bach liegt, hat unser Tor gemacht. Edna, die jeder kennt, redet den ganzen Tag. Der Bus hatte Verspätung, was uns geärgert hat. Mrs Birkett, der ich den Brief gegeben habe, sagt danke.
translation.it: Keswick, che è a otto miglia da qui, ha un museo delle matite. Mr Dixon, la cui fucina è vicino al torrente, ha fatto il nostro cancello. Edna, che tutti conoscono, parla tutto il giorno. L'autobus era in ritardo, il che ci ha fatto arrabbiare. Mrs Birkett, a cui ho dato la lettera, ringrazia.
translation.en: Keswick, which is eight miles from here, has a pencil museum. Mr Dixon, whose smithy is by the beck, made our gate. Edna, who everybody knows, talks all day. The bus was late, which made us cross. Mrs Birkett, to whom I gave the letter, says thank you.
